proposal.utterance: Classify 'a legal duty' in BFO top-level terms. Is it a continuant or an occurrent, and what subtype?

entities.label: LegalDuty
entities.rationale: A legal duty is a specifically dependent continuant: it cannot exist without inhering in a bearer (a person, organization, or other agent obligated by it). It is externally grounded — it arises from legal norms, institutional recognition, and relational facts about the bearer within a legal system — not from any intrinsic physical constitution of the bearer. This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition (BFO_0000016). It persists through time (continuant), does not have mass or spatial extent of its own (not an independent continuant), and is not a process or temporal region (not an occurrent). Note that working:LegalObligation already exists in the ontology with the same typing (BFO_0000023). LegalDuty may be considered a synonym or near-synonym of LegalObligation; see open_questions.

relations.rationale: LegalDuty is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in an agent, externally grounded in legal-institutional facts.

open_questions: working:LegalObligation already exists typed as BFO_0000023 (Role). Should 'LegalDuty' be treated as a synonym and mapped to that existing class (i.e., no new class minted), or is there an intended distinction between a duty and an obligation in this ontology (e.g., duty as a narrower Hohfeldian category vs. obligation as broader)?
Should LegalDuty be modeled as a subclass of working:LegalObligation, or as a sibling class under BFO_0000023?
Is the bearer of a legal duty restricted to persons/agents (BFO_0000040), or can institutional entities also bear legal duties in this ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: A legal duty is a CONTINUANT, specifically a Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), and within that branch it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023). The argument: (1) It is not an occurrent — it does not unfold or happen in time as a process; it persists through time while the agent remains obligated. (2) It is not an independent continuant — it has no mass, no spatial extent of its own, and cannot exist without a bearer. (3) Among specifically dependent continuants, it is a Role rather than a Quality or Disposition because its ground is external: it is conferred by legal norms, institutional recognition, and relational facts (e.g., being party to a contract, being subject to a jurisdiction), not by the intrinsic constitution of the bearer. This aligns with BFO_0000023 (Role). The ontology already contains working:LegalObligation typed identically; the user should clarify whether LegalDuty is a synonym, subtype, or distinct concept before committing a new class.
